matt_m.backstory:
Newly minted real estate agent, which means he is currently in the drumming-up-business phase and everyone in the WhatsApp knows it. Comes to it honestly — Airbnb operator, commercial brokering, a real track record — but there is no version of this where the group lets a fresh license go unremarked. Ohio born, Browns first, Buckeyes second, Cleveland everything after that. Trades movie and comedy recommendations with Zach at a volume that suggests neither of them has other hobbies, and their taste is bad in exactly the same way, which is why it works.

He is the only man in this group whose portrait has no school on it at all. Everyone else got a program; Matt got a billboard advertising his own phone number. He has never once complained about this, which is the most damning part of it.

The board is three unders and one over, which is a man walking you through comps. Vanderbilt under 5.5 is the sharp one and he knows it: the market took two good years and priced them as a permanent condition, and permanent conditions are exactly what he sells against. North Carolina under 4.5 is the same trade with the volume turned up. Texas Tech under 10.5 is the one that will hurt — he faded the one program in the country that went out and actually paid for a roster, which is a thing he would have noticed in any other business. Penn State over 8.5 is the listing, and he believes in the listing.
matt_m.running_gag: The hustle. Every conversation eventually becomes a listing.
matt_m.draft_tendency: Sells you on his picks. Hard. Three of the four are unders, so what he is mostly selling is nothing happening.
matt_m.fatal_flaw: Cannot tell the difference between a thing being cheap and a thing being bad — a fine instinct in real estate, an expensive one here.

hauck.backstory:
Hosts the game, which grants him diplomatic immunity roughly none of the time. Works in alcohol, tastes wine seriously, lifts, and walks his lab nearly every day — a genuinely well-rounded life that he then spends every autumn feeding into the Cleveland Browns. Ohio born and Ohio State made, which at this table is the rare credential: most of this group roots for things they picked up somewhere along the way, and Hauck actually comes from the place he roots for. He has the receipts, he knows he has the receipts, and he will produce them unprompted. He married a veterinarian, which given the dog situation reads less like romance and more like vertical integration.

Which makes the portrait a problem, because they put him in Kentucky blue. He took Kentucky over 4.5 and has been explaining it ever since: a four-and-a-half win floor in the SEC is not a projection, it is an insult, and somebody at this table was going to take the other side of an insult. Nobody asked him to become a Wildcat about it. He has leaned in anyway, the way he leans into everything.

Ohio State over 9.5 is the honest one and the only pick he does not have to argue for. Navy over 7.5 is the tasting-flight pour — he likes an offense nobody gets a real practice week against. Miami under 10.5 is the bottle he sent back: a ceiling that tall resting that heavily on staying healthy is not a bet, it is a hope, and he does not drink hope.
hauck.running_gag: The receipts. He has them, he knows he has them, and he will produce them.
hauck.draft_tendency: Curated. Treats a draft board like a tasting flight.
hauck.fatal_flaw: Confuses a number being disrespectful with a number being wrong.

bryan.backstory:
The youngest at the table and the best player at it, which is an annoying combination to sit across from. Runs his own PE group, engaged to Samantha, neighbor to Zach, owner of a brown lab named Tater, and — the detail that undoes all of the above — an enthusiastic decorator of his home with ferns. The man has a green thumb. He is also a deeply serious Ohio State and Browns fan and takes an enormous amount of incoming for it. Takes it well. Then takes Zach’s money.

They rendered him in Virginia colors. Not one person, Bryan included, has produced an explanation. He does not have a Virginia opinion. He has never had a Virginia opinion. He is now, permanently, a Cavalier.

The board is a leveraged buyout. He shorted Michigan at 8.5 and Texas at 9.5 — the two most-hyped brands in the sport — and rolled the proceeds into Kent State over 3.5 and South Florida over 8.5. Two names sold at the top, two small caps bought at the bottom. The Michigan under is the one place where the model and the Ohio State fan in him agreed completely, and he has never looked more at peace. South Florida over 8.5 is the one his day job should have talked him out of: that is buying a mid-major after the good year, at the number the good year created. It is also the only head-to-head on this board — Todd has the under — so two men who have never once cared about South Florida will now watch every snap of it for exactly opposite reasons.
bryan.draft_tendency: Ruthless. Reads the board and doesn't blink.
bryan.fatal_flaw: Will always take the clever side of a trade, including the times the obvious side was the correct one.

todd.backstory:
The most relaxed man in the group by a wide margin. Works support at Autodesk, drives a Rivian, and owns an enormous black lab mix named Atlas who is, by consensus, the largest dog anyone here has met. Die-hard Browns, which for a laid-back guy means he has developed a serenity the rest of the group has not — decades of practice at accepting outcomes. Jokes constantly, never escalates.

He is the only manager with two portraits and both of them put him in Ohio State red. He then built a board with not one Big Ten team on it. Wears the shirt, will not back the conference, and sees no tension in this whatsoever.

What he does back is a ceiling. Boise State over 7.5 and Iowa State over 4.5 are the same pick made twice: programs that have quietly cleared those numbers again and again while the market kept filing it under surprise. The Iowa State over is close to free and he took it in about four seconds. Then he turned around and put unders on South Florida and James Madison, which is where the thesis comes apart — James Madison is a group-of-five program that reloads, and fading it is the exact bet he spent the other half of his board arguing against. The South Florida under is this board’s only head-to-head, with Bryan on the other side. The most relaxed man in the group has been handed the one pick he cannot be relaxed about. He intends to be relaxed about it anyway.
todd.running_gag: The dog. The Rivian. The unbotherable calm.
todd.draft_tendency: Doesn't overthink. Picks and moves on.
todd.fatal_flaw: Holds two opposite theories about group-of-five football at the same time and has never once been troubled by it.

zach.backstory:
Wake Forest, LSU, and the only man at this table who does not care about the Cleveland Browns, which is its own kind of standing. Built the entire scoring engine, projection model and website for a pool that could have run on a napkin. Contributes reliably at poker in the sense that his money reliably ends up elsewhere, mostly Bryan’s. Has decided that the correct response to being bad at one game is to build a second game and administer it.

His portrait is the only one that is not a sideline. It is a press conference, behind a Wake Forest podium, under a nameplate reading FAT ZACH — HEAD COACH. He is the one man here whose art is his actual school and the one man here who did not draft it. Wake Forest opened at a number he has called defensible, which is the word he uses when the model disagrees with him and he has decided to let it win.

Four picks, four overs, from the person who wrote the projection model — which makes the commissioner the single most optimistic man in a league he built himself. He says the numbers told him to. He wrote the numbers. LSU over 8.5 is at least honest; that one is just his school. Oregon over 10.5 is the one that should worry him, because asking a team for eleven wins is not optimism, it is a toll you pay in November.
zach.running_gag: Loses at poker, writes the scoring for everything else.
zach.draft_tendency: Overthinks it, then takes the model's number anyway.
zach.fatal_flaw: Built the model, trusts the model, and drafted the four teams the model liked best — which is either rigor or a closed loop, and he cannot tell you which.

josh.backstory:
They rendered him as a Stanford coach, and the longer you look at his board the more that reads as casting rather than coincidence. Stanford over 3.5 is a pick nobody else at this table would touch: a program the market has stopped believing in altogether, priced at a floor so low that Josh looked at it and saw a job worth taking. He is the only manager here who bought hope at the bottom.

Everything else is him taking the other side of teams people feel fine about. Florida under 7.5 and BYU under 8.5 are both bets that one decent season gets remembered as a trend, and he does not think either roster can run it back. The BYU under is the sharp one — that number is built almost entirely on a year where every close game fell the right way, and close games do not stay bought. Virginia over 7.5 is his second buy and the shakier of the two, because it asks a program to hold a level it has reached exactly once.

The through-line is a man who does not trust the middle. He wants a floor he can lift or a ceiling he can bet against, and he has no interest whatsoever in the teams everyone already agrees about.
josh.running_gag: Sees a rebuild everywhere. Has never once picked a team that was already good.
josh.draft_tendency: Buys the floor, fades the consensus. Nothing in the middle.
josh.fatal_flaw: Mistakes a low number for an opportunity, which is the same instinct that makes a man take the Stanford job in the first place.

mark.backstory:
His portrait puts him in Indiana crimson wearing a national championship patch, for a program that has never won one. Nobody has settled whether that is a joke at his expense or the single most accurate thing on this site.

Indiana over 10.5 is his whole board in one pick. Everyone else looked at a program that had one impossible season and called it lightning; Mark looked at the same season and decided it was a thing that had actually happened and could therefore happen again. Eleven wins is an enormous ask and he did not blink at it. Duke over 5.5 is the same instinct with less on the line — he thinks that staff is better than its number, and he is probably right.

The unders are where he turns skeptical instead of hopeful, and both are aimed at programs the sport cannot stop talking about. Notre Dame under 11.5 fades the annual assumption that Notre Dame is one game away from everything. Maryland under 5.5 is the quiet one and the likeliest to cash. It is a strange, coherent board: he doubts the famous and believes the improbable, which is a difficult way to live and an excellent way to draft.
mark.running_gag: Believes. Loudly, and about things there is no reason to believe about.
mark.draft_tendency: Backs the improbable, fades the famous.
mark.fatal_flaw: Cannot distinguish between a season that proved something and a season that merely happened.
